title: Transport Minister resigns citing health, first cabinet exit of the Fujimori government
detail: Transport and Communications Minister Rafael Rey resigned, citing health reasons that prevented him from continuing 'the responsibilities proper to the position with the dedication it requires' — the first departure from Keiko Fujimori's cabinet since it was sworn in July 28. Congressman Víctor Piñán suggested the real cause was linked to trains acquired during Rafael López Aliaga's tenure as Lima mayor. The resignation came days after Fujimori had publicly dismissed opposition-fueled 'speculation' about an imminent cabinet reshuffle, denying any changes were being evaluated 'for now.' President Fujimori swore in economist José Angello Tangherlini Casal, previously vice-minister of Family Agriculture Development, as the new Transport and Communications Minister the same day; his mandatory sworn declaration disclosed three active fiscal investigations for alleged embezzlement of funds (malversación) and official extortion (concusión) from his time at Agro Rural, none yet closed, dismissed or resolved.

media.caption: Fujimori names José Angelo Tangherlini Casal as Transport Minister after the first cabinet resignation

title: IEP poll: Fujimori approval at 37% after less than two months in office
detail: A national survey by the Instituto de Estudios Peruanos (IEP), fielded September 4–10 and presented exclusively by RPP, put President Keiko Fujimori's approval at 37% against 49% disapproval (14% undecided). 52% of respondents said her government is 'more of the same,' versus 33% who see it as real change, and 47% consider her poorly or not at all prepared to govern. Congress fared worse, with only 20% approval against 65% disapproval. A separate Datum poll reported Fujimori's approval falling 18 points in her first month in office.

media.caption: IEP September survey puts Fujimori's approval at 37%

title: BCRP cuts 2026 growth forecast on El Niño, chief warns new AFP withdrawal would 'destroy' pension system
detail: Presenting the central bank's September Reporte de Inflación, BCRP president Julio Velarde cut Peru's 2026 GDP growth forecast from 3.4% to 3.2% and 2027's from 3.2% to 3%, citing the impact of the El Niño phenomenon on productive sectors and inflationary pressure. Velarde also criticized a new bill — presented September 18 by congresswoman Catherin Palomino of Juntos por el Perú in the newly bicameral Congress — that would allow a ninth extraordinary withdrawal from private pension funds (AFPs), this time justified by a possible El Niño-driven economic crisis. 'Every country in the world has a pension system; here we're destroying it,' Velarde said.

media.caption: BCRP president Julio Velarde presents the September Reporte de Inflación
